segments: A man owed the king ten thousand talents. Since he had no way to pay, the king ordered that his wife and children be sold along with all his possessions.
But the debtor fell to his knees before the king and began to plead with him, "Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything." The king took pity on him and forgave his debt.
The debtor, after leaving the king, met his friend, who owed him only a hundred dinars. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, "Give me what you owe."
The friend fell to his knees and started begging, "Just wait a little longer and I'll give you everything back." But the other one didn't want to wait and had him thrown in jail
When the king learned of this, he summoned a cruel servant and said to him, "Wicked servant, I forgave you because you begged me.
"Shouldn't you have forgiven your friend as well?" The king got angry and ordered that the wicked servant be thrown into prison until he pays off his entire debt
So will My Heavenly Father do to you if each of you does not forgive his brother from his heart for his offenses.

master_scene_en: In a serene, sunlit setting reminiscent of the early 1st century in Judea, a man with long dark hair and a well-groomed beard stands with a calm yet intense expression. He wears a simple, flowing white tunic made of fine linen, cinched at the waist with a modest rope belt. The tunic drapes elegantly over his shoulders, with sleeves that fall just below the elbows, revealing his strong forearms. His feet are bare, connecting him to the earth beneath him. The background features a rustic mill interior, with rough stone walls and beams of light filtering through small openings, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. Dust particles dance in the light shafts, enhancing the sense of tranquility. The man stands in a relaxed yet authoritative posture, his gaze directed slightly downward, embodying compassion and wisdom. As he begins to speak, the light softly illuminates his face, highlighting the depth of his expression. He speaks in a gentle yet firm tone, saying: "A man owed the king ten thousand talents. Since he had nothing to pay, the king ordered that he be sold, along with his wife and children and all his possessions. But the debtor fell on his knees before the king and begged him, 'Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything.' The king had compassion on him and forgave him the debt. But when that same debtor went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay what you owe.' So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, 'Have patience with me, and I will pay you.' He refused and went and put him in prison until he should pay the debt. When the king heard about this, he called the servant and said to him, 'You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me. And should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?' And in anger, his master delivered him to the jailers, until he should pay all his debt. So also my heavenly Father will do to every one of you, if you do not forgive your brother from your heart.'"
voice_description: His voice is calm and authoritative, conveying deep compassion and wisdom, resonating with the emotional weight of the message.
quote_caption_ru:
"Один человек был должен царю десять тысяч талантов. Так как ему нечем было заплатить, то царь велел продать его жену и детей и все его имения.

Но должник упал на колени перед царем и стал просить его: потерпи на мне, я все заплачу тебе». Царь пожалел его и простил ему долг.

Должник же, выйдя от царя, встретил своего друга, который должен был ему только сто динариев схватил его и начал душить, говоря: «отдай мне что должен».

Друг упал на колени и стал просить: «потерпи немного и все отдам тебе». Но тот не хотел ждать и посадил его в тюрьму.

Царь, когда узнал об этом, то призвал к себе жестокого раба и сказал ему: «злой раб, я простил тебе, потому что ты упросил меня. 

Не нужно ли было бы и тебе простить своего друга»? Царь рассердился и приказал посадить злого раба в тюрьму, пока он не выплатит весь свой долг.

Так и Отец Мой Небесный поступит с вами, если не простит каждый из вас от сердца своего брату своему согрешений его." – Иисус Христос
quote_caption_en: "A man owed the king ten thousand talents. Since he had nothing to pay, the king ordered that he be sold, along with his wife and children and all his possessions. But the debtor fell on his knees before the king and begged him, 'Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything.' The king had compassion on him and forgave him the debt. But when that same debtor went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay what you owe.' So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, 'Have patience with me, and I will pay you.' He refused and went and put him in prison until he should pay the debt. When the king heard about this, he called the servant and said to him, 'You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me. And should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?' And in anger, his master delivered him to the jailers, until he should pay all his debt. So also my heavenly Father will do to every one of you, if you do not forgive your brother from your heart." – Jesus Christ

Царь рассердился и приказал посадить злого раба в тюрьму, пока он не выплатит весь свой долг. Так и Отец Мой Небесный поступит с вами, если не простит каждый из вас от сердца своего брату своему согрешений его.
script_en: A man owed the king ten thousand talents. Since he had nothing to pay, the king ordered that he be sold, along with his wife and children and all his possessions. But the debtor fell on his knees before the king and begged him, 'Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything.' The king had compassion on him and forgave him the debt. But when that same debtor went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay what you owe.' So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, 'Have patience with me, and I will pay you.' He refused and went and put him in prison until he should pay the debt. When the king heard about this, he called the servant and said to him, 'You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me. And should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?' And in anger, his master delivered him to the jailers, until he should pay all his debt. So also my heavenly Father will do to every one of you, if you do not forgive your brother from your heart.
